audit.why: FAV fits 55.12%: Trundle has no gap-closer and no ranged tool, so Mini Gnar dictates every trade, and his comeback is the late-game drain rather than the lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five chart rows disagreed with their own whys. whys[0] says Mini wins the first trade (stored Trundle), whys[1] calls level 2 a free chunky trade (stored Skill), whys[3] calls Levels 4-5 'a coinflip on Rage' (stored Gnar), whys[4] says a Rage-up level 6 'kills Trundle outright' (stored Trundle), whys[6] says he reclaims the duel and you win as an engager instead (stored Gnar).
audit.why: The packet chart (Gnar/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Gnar/Gnar/Skill) matches the prose row for row. Spikes are otherwise right: Gnar level 2, Rage-gated 4-5, Gnar at 6 with a wall behind him, first item, then Trundle's Subjugate window late.
audit.corrected: win[0]=Gnar, win[1]=Gnar, win[3]=Skill, win[4]=Gnar, win[6]=Skill with matching phases sides and phases[6].why rewritten. One atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Pillar of Ice purely as something done TO you ('walls your kite path'). It is impassable terrain — which means it is also a wall for GNAR!. Gnar can fling Trundle into Trundle's own pillar for the bonus damage and the extended stun. Nothing on the page says so. Chomp's auto-attack reset is also unmentioned, and Subjugate is described only as 'steals your stats' with no numbers.
audit.why: The pillar reversal is the single highest-value trick in this matchup and turns his best zoning tool into your kill setup. The Chomp reset is the burst tell that tells you when to step back.
audit.corrected: Pillar of Ice (E, 21s at rank 1, 1000 range) is impassable terrain and therefore a valid wall for GNAR! — bait it and fling him into it. Chomp (Q, 3.5s, 300 range) is an auto-attack reset that saps your AD, so the wind-up is the cue, not the cast. Frozen Domain (W, 18s at rank 1) gives attack speed, move speed and amplified healing — never brawl on it. Subjugate (R, 120s at rank 1) steals health, armour and MR, then doubles the theft over four seconds, so raw resistances are the wrong answer.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Trundle carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Late he reclaims the duel — Subjugate strips resists and he out-sustains you, so win as the engager, not the 1v1.

edits.before: Mega Wallop into GNAR! against a wall is your kill window with no dash for Trundle to escape — but only commit on Rage, or his E pillar walls your kite path and his W zone runs you down in Mini.
edits.after: Mega Wallop into GNAR! against a wall is your kill window — and his own Pillar of Ice is terrain, so his E can be the wall you stun him into. Commit only on Rage, or that pillar cuts your kite instead.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the swing. If Rage lines up, Mega lets you Wallop-stun and, with a wall behind him, GNAR! him into it for a long stun and big damage — a clean kill against a champ with no dash out. But if you're stuck in Mini with Rage on cooldown, his E pillar can wall off your retreat and his W zone (move speed plus attack speed and healing) lets him run you down and drain — that's the one path he wins this lane. Only commit when Mega is up and terrain is behind him.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are the swing. If Rage lines up, Mega lets you Wallop-stun and, with terrain behind him, GNAR! him into it for a long stun and big damage — and his own Pillar of Ice (E, 21s at rank 1) is impassable terrain, so bait it and fling him into his own wall. Stuck in Mini with Rage down, that same pillar cuts your retreat while his W zone runs you down and drains. Chomp is an auto reset on 3.5s: the wind-up is your cue to step back.

edits.before: Steals your stats. Avoid the brawl. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Subjugate is 120s at rank 1 — take your all-in while it is still down.

edits.before: That is Trundle's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Frozen Domain gives him attack speed, move speed and amplified healing — 18s.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Subjugate takes health, armour and MR, then doubles it over 4s.

notes: Best find here: Pillar of Ice is impassable terrain, so it is a valid wall for GNAR!. The page only ever described the pillar as something that traps Gnar; it can be the wall you stun Trundle into, which is exactly what the mirror recorded from Trundle's side. Also added the Chomp auto-reset tell and real Subjugate numbers, covering the flagged autoreset-burst-tell and resistances-invalidated gaps. Data caveat carried over from the mirror: the packet and the on-disk content file disagree on win rate and games for this matchup (packet 55.12 / 205 here, the mirror saw 47.8 / 159 on its packet and 44.88 / 205 on disk). I did not touch any win-rate field. I used the packet level chart only because the on-disk whys independently agree with it.
